War, Rates & Real Estate: Should You Buy a Home in 2026 or Wait?

Mortgage rates, negotiating power and neighborhood-level value: a Tucson perspective on the decision to buy or wait.

By Reddy Appraisal LLCOctober 21, 20263 min read

IN THIS ARTICLE

Why the decision feels harder in 2026The balance between negotiating power and financing costsStart with your budget and the local marketMore in Buying a Home ↗← All 24 articles

THE SHORT ANSWER

Start with the payment you can comfortably afford today, including taxes, insurance, maintenance, and an emergency cushion. Think about how long you'll stay and whether the home fits your needs without depending on a future refinance.

Why the decision feels harder in 2026

If you've been waiting for the perfect time to buy a home, 2026 probably hasn't made the decision easy. The ongoing conflict involving Iran has added uncertainty to energy prices and inflation, while mortgage rates have climbed. Freddie Mac reported an average 30-year fixed rate of 7.40% on October 15, 2026, compared with 6.27% a year earlier. That's a real difference in monthly payments, and it's understandable that some buyers are pressing pause. But does a challenging market automatically mean it's a bad time to buy? Not necessarily.

The balance between negotiating power and financing costs

Here's the upside that doesn't always make the headlines: when fewer buyers are shopping, the ones who remain may have more room to negotiate. Depending on the neighborhood and property, that could mean a lower purchase price, seller-paid closing costs, or time to make a thoughtful decision instead of rushing into a bidding war. The trade-off? Higher financing costs can outweigh those savings, and home values can still move down. Waiting might help your budget, but lower rates aren't guaranteed - and if rates do fall, competition could return.

Start with your budget and the local market

So should you buy now or wait? Start with the payment you can comfortably afford today, including taxes, insurance, maintenance, and an emergency cushion. Think about how long you'll stay and whether the home fits your needs without depending on a future refinance. In Tucson and across Southern Arizona, neighborhood-level pricing matters far more than any national headline. An independent appraisal can help you understand a property's market value before making a major commitment. You can't control the headlines, but you can make a well-informed decision.
